The index groups corpora by language and type, covering English (North American, African American and UK), Chinese, Japanese, Germanic, Romance, Slavic (including Czech) and other languages, plus bilingual, clinical and narrative collections and derived frequency corpora. The CLAN program and the browsable TalkBankDB search work with the transcripts.

notes: Transcripts and media need a free TalkBank account; clinical corpora need approved access. Each use must cite at least one corpus reference from the corpus page and acknowledge the CHILDES grant (NICHD HD082736). The TalkBank Ground Rules license the data under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, which "precludes the incorporation of the data in commercial products, including systems such as large language models (LLMs) such as ChatGPT". On web processing, data "can only be uploaded for processing by OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Rev-AI and similar systems if the user has specifically selected the option for non-storage of data": "Help improve Claude" off for Anthropic, "improve the model for everyone" off for OpenAI, Gemini Apps Activity off for Google. Local analysis has no such limit. Identifiable data may "only be stored on a local device for analysis and cannot be circulated further". In November 2026 the CHILDES home page said the repository was "under review for potential modification in compliance with Administration directives", so record the date and version of any download.

title: Memory of Nations (Paměť národa) oral history archive
provider: Post Bellum, with Czech Radio and the Institute for the Study of Totalitarian Regimes
licence_name: Terms for reuse of recordings not published on the open pages
data: Recorded life-story interviews with witnesses of 20th-century history, mostly in Czech. On 22 Nov 2026 the site listed 22,315 witnesses in the database, 12,723 published witness stories, 74,219 clips and 189,954 photographs. Published stories combine audio or video clips with written summaries.
found_context: Searched for downloadable interview audio and video for analysis
notes: Clips play on the public site. Full recordings are offered through a researcher area (e-badatelna) that needs a login; 23,101 researchers were registered. The open pages hold only a privacy notice, so the terms for downloading recordings and analysing them with models need to be asked of Post Bellum before use. Interviews contain personal life histories; treat them as personal data.

Quoting or presenting clips in publications has its own permission rules on the citation page, which also gives the required credit lines.

title: Seamless Interaction dataset
licence_name: CC BY-NC 4.0
data: Over 4,000 hours of face-to-face conversation between more than 4,000 participants, recorded as one video and audio track per participant, in naturalistic and improvised (role-played) sessions. Each file comes with a transcript, voice-activity timing and extracted movement, face and body-pose features. Distributed as WebDataset archives of about 1 GB; a sample set is about 1 GB and the whole dataset about 27 TB.
found_context: Searched for downloadable interview audio and video for analysis
notes: No account is needed. Non-commercial use with attribution. Participants were recruited through vendors in several sites, and the card notes variation in production quality and in the accuracy of annotated time stamps. Pair the two participant files of an interaction to see both sides.

title: Seshat: Global History Databank
licence_name: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Public Data, under the Seshat User Agreement)
data: Coded variables on the social and political organisation of past societies, recorded per polity and period. The database lists 867 polities in 47 regions, with general, social complexity, warfare, religion and economy variables, plus crisis and instability datasets. Public releases include replication datasets, the Polaris-2026 snapshot (spreadsheet, on GitHub), the earlier Equinox-2020 spreadsheet and an API with Python packages.

notes: Browsing needs no account; downloading CSV or JSON needs a free account and acceptance of the User Agreement. Work-in-progress (Private) data may be visible but must not be shared. Values are expert codings with stated uncertainty, so results depend on the release used; cite the release.

title: TalkBank

data: Transcribed spoken-language corpora in 14 research areas and over 42 languages, in the CHAT transcription format, often with linked audio or video. The Ground Rules forbid commercial use, including in language models, and uploading data to web processing services unless non-storage is selected. Cite each corpus as its manual says. The site links a CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 deed while the text says 4.0.
